Overview

This page renders the VI Foundry proof machinery. Simulacra sections summarize parameter-recovery tests on synthetic data with known ground truth (STDD). The Baseline Oracle section shows every §12 manuscript result with its tolerance band, and the Key Results section reproduces the README results table (T1-T7, formal model, L3).

1. Simulacra Overview

Each simulacrum runs the pipeline on synthetic data with known parameters (true params) and verifies the pipeline recovers them (recovered params) within the credible interval. The null control confirms the pipeline does not recover when no signal is present (specificity).

3. Baseline Oracle (§12 results)

Every value below is the manuscript-reported result, stored as ground truth in baseline/oracle.yml. The regression CI gate compares pipeline output to these values within numerical tolerance.

TestPredictionKey valueSupports VIDistinguishes VICaveat
T1: Orobanchaceae PGLSPlastome size correlates with parasitism levelbeta = -23.5, r_squared = 0.652, p_value = 1.25e-09, n_species = 12YesNoRelaxed selection predicts the same gradient. Caveat in paper §12.1.2.
T2: Cross-family replicationFamily-mean plastome size correlates with family-mean parasitism across independent parasitic lineages (between-family association)pearson_r = -0.934, FALSE = 15, p_value = 1.39e-41YesNoAlso predicted by relaxed selection on photosynthetic genes.
T3: Endosymbiont biphasicGenome reduction follows biphasic kinetics (fast then slow)r_squared = 0.92, k1_k2_ratio = 19, bayes_factor = 6.7YesYesn=10 genera; sensitivity to individual data points not fully tested.
T4: Niche vs NeNiche breadth predicts gene loss better than Ne aloneniche_r_squared = 0.343, ne_r_squared = 0.198YesYes—
T5: Pan-genome fluidityPan-genome openness tracks lifestyle (commensal vs free-living)—YesYes—
T6: Gene-loss orderingIntegration-depth determines gene-loss orderspearman_orobanchaceae = 0.955, spearman_cuscuta = 0.986, cross_family_concordance = 0.941, permutation_p = 0.0083, quasibinomial_p = 1e-04, pseudo_r_squared = 0.82YesYes—
T7: LTEE co-segregationFunction-loss mutations co-segregate with beneficial mutations LESS than chance (passive drift in unused genes)observed_pct = 36.4, expected_pct = 61.7, p_value = 1e-04YesNoHitchhiking confound; arbitrary window; misspecified null. Reported as suggestive.
Formal modelBiphasic kinetics: fast Phase 1 (unprotected traits shed), slow Phase 2 (protected traits retained)phase1_rate = 1, phase2_rate = 3.559e-06, early_late_displacement_ratio = 280981, threshold_biphasicity = 1YesYesDeterministic ODE outputs (final_retention = [~0, ~0, ~0, 1, 1] for depths [0,1,2,3,5] with theta=2.5). Not empirical — see T3 for the empirical biphasic test.
empirical_formal_modelAdditive GLM (retention ~ dep + para): dep > 0 (protected), para < 0 (shed); cross-kingdom rho > 0dep_coefficient = 0.8375, dep_p_value = 0.0007557, para_coefficient = -1.864, para_p_value = 3.502e-05, pseudo_r_squared = 0.5515, cross_kingdom_rho = 0.7545, cross_kingdom_p = 0.03051YesYesEmpirical GLM fit to the 8x6 retention matrix (corrected flattening, Remark R7). The foundry's theoretical ODE (threshold_model) is the companion simulation; this is the empirical test that can fail.
L3: Cross-kingdom transferPlant-derived slope SIGN predicts bird morphological change ordering (ordering-concordance transfer; slope magnitude does not transfer)bird_rho = 0.755, bird_p = 0.031YesYesOrdering transfers across kingdoms; rate does not.

4. Key Results

Reproduced from the README. Every value is confirmed in baseline/oracle.yml.

TestWhat it measuresKey valueDistinguishes VI from competitors?
T1Orobanchaceae PGLSPlastome genome size vs parasitism depthβ = −23.5 kb/level, R² = 0.652, p < 10⁻⁹No — relaxed selection predicts the same gradient
T2Cross-family replicationGene-loss gradient replicates across lineagesPearson r = −0.934, n = 91, p = 1.39e-41No — also predicted by relaxed selection on photosynthetic genes
T3Endosymbiont biphasicGenome reduction kinetics shapeR² = 0.920, BF = 6.7 (logistic vs exponential)Yes — constant-rate and ratchet predict different shapes
T4Niche vs NeNiche breadth predicts gene loss better than Ne aloneNiche R² = 0.343 vs Ne R² = 0.198Yes — drift-only model predicts Ne dominates
T5Pan-genome fluidityPan-genome openness tracks lifestyleLifestyle subsumes NeYes — Ne-only model predicts no lifestyle signal
T6Gene-loss orderingFunctional dependency vs retention orderρ = 0.955, exact permutation p = 0.0083Yes — random loss predicts no ordering
T7LTEE co-segregationFunction-loss depleted near beneficial sweepsObserved 36.4% vs expected 61.7%, p = 0.0001 (depletion, not enrichment)No — hitchhiking confound; reported as suggestive
FMFormal modelBiphasic kinetics: fast Phase 1, slow Phase 2Phase1 rate 19.0, Phase2 rate 1.0, R² = 0.920, BF = 6.7Yes — constant-rate and accelerating models fit worse
L3Cross-kingdom transferPlant parameters predict bird morphologyρ = 0.755, p = 0.031Yes — substrate independence predicts no transfer
